subject: Russia
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about Kaliningrad Oblast. Claims are cited to pinned Wikipedia revisions (trusted_secondary). The oblast is called a semi-exclave because it has a Baltic coast. Its city points are approximate (taken to the nearest minute of the article).

claims.text: Kaliningrad Oblast is the westernmost federal subject of Russia.
The oblast is a semi-exclave on the Baltic Sea, bordered by Poland to the south, Lithuania to the north and east, and the Baltic Sea to the west.
The port town of Baltiysk is Russia's only port on the Baltic Sea that remains ice-free in winter.
Kaliningrad Oblast had a population of roughly one million in the 2021 Russian census.

The territory was formerly the northern part of East Prussia and overwhelmingly inhabited by Germans; after the defeat of Nazi Germany in World War II the Soviet Union annexed the region into the Russian SFSR.
In 1255 the Teutonic Order founded the city of Königsberg, modern Kaliningrad, on the foundations of a destroyed Sambian settlement.

kaliningrad.note: Kaliningrad, the oblast’s largest city and administrative centre.

baltiysk.note: Baltiysk, the ice-free port on the Baltic coast.
